narration.text: An all-nighter can impair your reactions like alcohol.
Here’s what happens, hour by hour.
Hour sixteen. Adenosine has been building all day, increasing the pressure to sleep.
By seventeen to nineteen hours, some test performance resembles point zero five percent blood alcohol.
Microsleeps can happen: brief, involuntary sleep you might not even notice.
At twenty-four hours, one study found performance like point one percent blood alcohol. Above most US driving limits.
Through the next day: at thirty-five hours, one study found about sixty percent greater amygdala reactivity to negative images.
A small study also found higher ghrelin and hunger after one sleepless night.
Coffee blocks adenosine’s signal. The sleep pressure is still there.
Recovery sleep helps. One long night can restore alertness, but some effects take longer.
What’s the longest you’ve stayed awake? Tell me in the comments.
